details.summary: This is a fresh, convenient, and mostly well-constructed assembly-only bowl that fits the diet's principles beautifully. However, the vinaigrette is far too acidic as written and must be balanced, and the fiber content needs a slight boost to meet the chapter's minimum floor.

dimensions.feedback: The vinaigrette ratio is extremely acidic—2 tablespoons of apple cider vinegar to only 2 teaspoons of olive oil is 3 parts acid to 1 part oil. This will be harshly sour. Change the dressing to equal parts: 1 tablespoon of extra-virgin olive oil and 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar. Additionally, consider adding a pinch of salt to the dressing since the recipe's overall sodium is very low (150 mg).
All ingredients are properly utilized in the instructions, and no unlisted ingredients appear in the steps.
The assembly steps are clear, logical, and provide all the necessary guidance for a no-cook dish.
The ingredients and flavor profile align perfectly with a Modern American salad bowl.
A no-cook, assembly-only method is perfectly suited for these pantry staples and fresh produce.
The computed nutrition values accurately reflect the ingredients and quantities provided.
The title and intro accurately describe the dish without making any banned health claims or using inappropriate diet language.
Once the dressing's acidity is balanced, this will be a highly appealing, crunchy, and refreshing meal that comes together effortlessly.

The recipe effectively combines lean protein, heart-healthy fats (walnuts, olive oil), and quality whole-grain carbohydrates (brown rice) with fresh produce, answering perfectly to the diet's core philosophy.
There is zero added sugar, with sweetness naturally provided by the whole apple. The brown rice supplies a high-quality, whole-grain carbohydrate base that fits comfortably within the target window.

The recipe misses the chapter's 6g fiber floor, providing only 5.3g per serving. To fix this without significantly increasing calories, increase the baby greens to 4 cups (120 g) and specify a 'large' crisp apple rather than a medium one.
The recipe requires zero cooking and uses ready-to-eat staples like cooked brown rice and canned salmon, making it incredibly practical and easily achievable in under 15 minutes.
